text:
Alex W: Heads-up — noticed a big dip in prefix cache hit-rate after the kernel selection change. Dashboard: https://perf.internal/runs/1867 — went from ~82% to ~39% for the chat api under medium-traffic load.
Maria S: ouch. do we know what keys changed? any tokenizer/version differences?
Kevin L: quick summary from profiler: cache key now includes raw system prompt + tokenizer version string + serialized function_call metadata. We also changed the JSON serializer in runtime (stable but different spacing/order).
Sophie R: aha — that serializer change would cause misses. we need canonicalization, not rely on the serializer output. small diffs break hashes.
perf-bot: nightly-kv-stats: canary-05%: hit_rate=38.4%, miss_rate=61.6%, avg_latency_tokens=12.1ms
Alex W: Agree. Proposal: compute cache fingerprint from canonicalized prompt structure instead of raw bytes. Fingerprint fields: model_id, quantization_tag, tokenizer_hash, canonical_prompt_hash. Exclude ephemeral fields like request_id, client_time, trace_id.
Maria S: For tokenizer_hash we should pin and record the tokenizer commit hash used at tokenization time. If tokenization algo changes, the fingerprint changes intentionally. But we should NOT include the human-readable tokenizer version string, only a short hash.
Kevin L: Also function/tool calls — we currently stringify "function_call": {name, args} preserving insertion order. Need to stable-serialize: sort object keys, normalize arrays, collapse insignificant whitespace. Example pseudocode:
```\ndef canonicalize_payload(payload):\n  remove_keys(payload, ["request_id", "client_time", "trace_id"])\n  if type(payload) == dict:\n    return \"{\" + \",\".join([k+\":\"+canonicalize_payload(payload[k]) for k in sorted(payload.keys())]) + \"}\"\n  if type(payload) == list:\n    return \"[\" + \",\".join([canonicalize_payload(x) for x in payload]) + \"]\"\n  return normalize_whitespace_and_unicode(str(payload))\n```
Sophie R: Also collapse repeated spaces, normalize unicode NFKC, remove zero-width chars. And for system prompt changes we should compute a separate system_prompt_hash and include it in tiered keying (so we can invalidate system prompts without evicting model/tokenizer combos).
Alex W: Good point — tiered key: primary=(model, tokenizer_hash, quant_tag), secondary=canonical_prompt_hash, tertiary=system_prompt_hash. Runtime can check primary-level matches before fetching warm KV entries for different system prompts.
Maria S: Did a small local canary: after canonicalization + tokenizer hash pin, hit-rate for our test harness went from 38% -> 84% on repeated conversational prefixes (same user messages, diff serialized metadata). I can paste numbers later.
Kevin L: Nice. We need backward-compat: existing entries keyed with old serializer won't match. Plan: warmup jobs that replay recent requests to repopulate new-key entries, plus a transitional lookup that attempts old-key -> rekey on miss for 24-48h. Tradeoff is extra latency on misses.
Sophie R: For rollouts: canary 5% for 24h, collect hit-rate, median latency, cost. If stable, ramp to 25% with warmup daemon prefill, then 100% after 72h.
Alex W: Risks: if tokenizer pinning differs across dedicated/private installs, we'll need per-customer tokenizer_hash map. Also watch for very common ephemeral fields we might have missed (sdk_client.version, feature-flag headers).
Maria S: I'll draft the normalization lib (python + go) and tests (roundtrip stability + fuzz). Will include test vectors for function calls with different key orders.
Kevin L: I'll add the transitional-lookup patch and the kernel change hook to include tokenizer commit id in logs.
Sophie R: I'll schedule the warmup daemon job and add metrics to the console (per-route cache hits by prompt-hash).
deploy-bot: deploy queued: event=canary-kv-canonicalization, targets=canary-05%, owner=Maria S
Alex W: Awesome. Maria — want to own the PR? :thumbsup:
Maria S: happy to. I'll open draft PR with the lib + tests and a rollout playbook.
Alex W: Thanks — we'll sync next on the perf dash.
Maria S: ping me if you have sample payloads that reproduce misses, I'll add them to test vectors.
